first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) support that reducing signup/onboarding friction reliably lifts activation and completion for self-serve/SMB accounts, without any noted data-quality caveats. This directly targets the internal metric decline rather than reacting to the competitor's pricing move. Promotional pricing (memory_73) looks tempting given the competitor threat, but that memory explicitly warns of a pooled-cohort redefinition mid-test, so its lift estimate is unreliable until verified against the archived record; racing on price also risks training price-sensitive segments toward low-margin behavior, working against sustainable qualified revenue. I'm spending verification budget on memory_73 to check whether the pooled-cohort issue invalidates or merely tempers its conclusion, and on memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-shortening result generalizes to the current account mix before committing this week's single experiment slot. Scale is kept at standard rather than broad rollout since this is a well-supported but not risk-free direction and we want a real read before scaling further.
